title: Winter Games
build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

records.c: The title screen, file T's entry, run by the loader at power-on. Copies the picture's colours from title_colours to colour RAM (1000 bytes, three pages and $E8 more), blacks out the border and the backgrounds, selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2, shows the bitmap at $4000 with its screen at $6000 ($D018 = $80), turns on bitmap and multicolour mode, waits three times title_wait and leaves through the loader's $0900, which the boot has pointed at the opening ceremony's load.
The high byte of the LDA $63E8,Y that copies the colours; title_start increases it after each page, with the store's at $3F09, so three passes copy $63E8-$66E7.
The high byte of the STA $D800,Y the colour copy writes through, increased with $3F06 after each page; the second loop at $3F16 copies the last 232 colours with plain addresses.

One of the title's three waits: 255 times 255 calls of title_poll at 63 cycles each with nothing pressed, 4.1 million cycles or about four seconds on a PAL machine; the whole title ran 13 seconds from its entry to the loader at $C0DC.

Reads both joysticks and the keyboard through CIA 1 ($DC00 AND $DC01, the low five bits): with nothing pressed it spends sixteen NOPs and returns; with a stick moved, fire or a key held it drops the two return addresses of title_wait and leaves the title at once through $0900.
105 bytes nothing reads, between the title's code and its picture: the contents of the author's memory saved with the file (the same pattern of $3F, $C0 and $FF bytes repeats at $5F98).
The title picture, a multicolour bitmap, 8 bytes per character cell and 320 to a row of cells. Rows 0-2: the purple "EPYX" logo and the first snowflake, top left.
Title bitmap rows 3-5: "PRESENTS" and the top of "WINTER".
Title bitmap rows 6-8: the middle of "WINTER", in white, blue and grey bands.
Title bitmap rows 9-11: the bottom of "WINTER" and the top of "GAMES".
Title bitmap rows 12-14: the top half of "GAMES" and the snowflakes left and right of it.
Title bitmap rows 15-17: the bottom half of "GAMES".
Title bitmap rows 18-20: "BY ACTION GRAPHICS" and a small snowflake.
Title bitmap rows 21-23: a snowflake, bottom right, and the top of the copyright line.
Title bitmap row 24: "© 1985 EPYX, Inc."
192 bytes after the bitmap that the video chip never shows and nothing reads: more of the author's memory saved with the file.
The title picture's screen memory, 1000 bytes, one per character cell: for each cell its two multicolour pairs, the colours of bit pairs 01 (high nybble) and 10 (low nybble).
The title picture's third colour for each of its 1000 cells (bit pair 11), which title_start copies to colour RAM.
The last 232 of the title picture's colours, rows 19 to 24, read as $66E8,Y by the second copy loop (title_colours holds the first 768).
The file's last byte, $45, one past the colours; nothing reads it.
